findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: doctor A has two blocks today (for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00). Expect exactly one row for A, with booked, free and next free counted across both blocks.
findings.text: REQ-2 says one row per doctor, and a doctor can have several availability blocks on one weekday. No AC gives a doctor two blocks today, so a join that outputs one row per block (duplicate rows, split counts) passes every S-1, S-3 and S-4 AC.

findings.text: Not fixed from attempt 1: S-7 AC2 and AC3 still compare to 'the same values as before this change' and name no expected values. The check depends on a pre-change baseline that the AC does not define.

rubric_items.reason: All 19 known REQs (REQ-1 to REQ-19) are traced by at least one story; there are no assumed REQs.
Stories are small, each with one clear outcome. S-1 groups listing, the time-zone rule, Inactive exclusion and the empty state, but they serve one outcome.

Prior F-1 is fixed: S-3 AC4 and S-4 AC5 now discriminate at the UTC+05:30 date boundary. Gaps remain: no doctor has two blocks on one weekday (duplicate rows), and S-7 compares to an undefined baseline.
Values are illustrative test data or come from the intent. UTC+05:30 and 22:30 UTC are derived inline from Asia/Kolkata (REQ-3), and 28 Nov 2026 is a Saturday.
Clear and consistent terms. The body restates the ACs in a shorter form that drops details (for example the Given in S-2 AC2), so it could drift from the front matter.
